title: Auth JeffersonWM shell layout pass
content:
Auth JeffersonWM received a shell-layout pass focused on making the signed-in /home workspace behave more like a real app surface and less like an early scaffold. The practical goal was to bring its frame closer to Stallioneer while also clarifying how the live deployment actually works.

What changed:

  • Shell frame aligned to Stallioneer: the Auth app now uses fixed top and bottom banners, the lighter page field, and matching left/right inset behavior so the outer structure sits in the same family as the newer utility apps.
  • Header copy simplified: the old eyebrow and long scaffold sentence were removed from the /home app shell, leaving the page framed more cleanly around the actual account tools.
  • Account workflow layout tightened: Your Account and Recent Activity were re-stacked and widened so they read as full working surfaces instead of narrow side-by-side cards.
  • Admin sections converted into accordions: Pending Requests, Approved Accounts, Blocked Accounts, and Deleted Accounts can now be opened and collapsed independently, which makes the moderation area less visually dense.
  • Future block preserved but disabled: the What Comes Next card was commented out instead of being deleted, so the planning copy can be restored later if needed.
  • Deployment reminder marker added: a build marker file was added to Auth so future builds visibly remind us to copy the rebuilt Auth dist into the live runtime folder on E:\auth-jeffersonwm\backend.

This pass also confirmed an important operational detail: live Auth is not updated through the usual static frontend copy path. The live /home route only changes after the rebuilt Auth app is copied into the home-server runtime and restarted there.
